Gerry McIlroy is the father of four-time major champion Rory McIlroy. A working-class man from Northern Ireland, Gerry made immense sacrifices to fund Rory’s early golf career, working multiple jobs including as a bartender at Holywood Golf Club. He introduced Rory to golf at age two and coached him until he was 17. Key Facts About Gerry McIlroy: Background: Grew up in public housing outside Belfast and played golf at a scratch-handicap level. Sacrifices: To pay for expensive tournament fees, Gerry worked 100-hour weeks, including cleaning toilets and bartending. Support: He supported Rory's dream completely, saying it was "always Rory's dream, not mine". Relationship: He has a very close bond with his son and is frequently seen celebrating at tournament wins. "£100k Bet": Gerry made headlines for a famous bet, placing £100 at 500-1 odds that his son would win an Open Championship within 10 years, which he won after Rory's 2014 victory. Gerry has a reputation for being a "kind, popular, and fun-loving" character.
